title: Classic Cheeseburger
description: The benchmark: a juicy 80/20 patty with melted American cheese on a toasted bun.
ingredients: ketchup and yellow mustard, to serve
steps: Divide the beef into 4 loose balls and flatten into patties slightly wider than the buns. Press a shallow dimple in the center so they stay flat.
Season both sides generously with salt and pepper right before cooking.
Heat a dry skillet or griddle over medium-high until it just starts to smoke. Cook the patties 3 minutes without moving them.
Flip, lay a slice of cheese on each, and cook 2-3 more minutes until the cheese slumps.
Butter the cut sides of the buns and toast them in the same pan for 1 minute.
Build: bottom bun, lettuce, patty, tomato, onion, condiments, top bun. Serve immediately.

title: Smash Burgers
description: Thin patties pressed hard onto a screaming-hot pan for lacy, crisp edges.
steps: Roll the beef into 8 loose golf balls. Do not compact them - looseness is what makes the crust.
Heat a cast-iron skillet over high heat for 4 minutes until lightly smoking.
Place 2 balls in the pan and immediately smash each flat with a sturdy spatula, pressing for a full 10 seconds.
Season, cook 90 seconds until the edges are deep brown and crisp, then scrape up with the spatula and flip.
Add cheese and cook 45 seconds more. Repeat with the rest.
Toast the buttered buns, spread with mayo and mustard, stack 2 patties per bun and add pickles.

title: Bacon Cheeseburger
description: Cheeseburger with crisp bacon and a smoky-sweet sauce.
steps: Cook the bacon in a cold skillet over medium heat until crisp, about 10 minutes. Move to paper towels and pour off all but 1 tbsp of fat.
Stir the mayo, barbecue sauce and smoked paprika together to make the sauce.
Form 4 patties slightly wider than the buns, dimple the centers and season both sides.
Cook in the bacon fat over medium-high, 3 minutes per side, adding cheddar after the flip.
Toast the buns cut-side down in the pan.
Spread sauce on both buns, then stack lettuce, patty, 2 slices of bacon and tomato.

title: Patty Melt
description: A diner classic: beef patty, deeply caramelized onions and Swiss griddled between rye.
steps: Melt 2 tbsp butter in a skillet over medium-low. Add the onions and a pinch of salt and cook 20-25 minutes, stirring now and then, until jammy and brown.
Scrape the onions into a bowl. Form the beef into 4 thin oval patties sized to the bread, and season.
Raise the heat to medium-high and cook the patties 2-3 minutes per side. Set aside.
Spread a thin layer of mayo on the outside of each bread slice - it browns more evenly than butter.
Build each sandwich: bread, cheese, patty, onions, cheese, bread.
Griddle over medium 3-4 minutes per side, pressing lightly, until the bread is crisp and the cheese has melted through.

title: Juicy Lucy
description: Minneapolis's cheese-stuffed burger - the molten center is the whole point.
ingredients: 4 slices American cheese, folded into squares
steps: Divide the beef into 8 equal balls and flatten each into a thin patty.
Set a folded cheese square in the middle of 4 patties, keeping it well clear of the edges.
Top with the remaining patties and pinch the edges together firmly all the way around. Any gap will leak. Season the outsides.
Cook in a skillet over medium - not high - heat for 5-6 minutes per side. Lower heat keeps the seam intact while the cheese melts.
Rest the burgers 3 minutes. This is not optional: the cheese comes out at lava temperature.
Serve on toasted buttered buns with pickles and mustard. Warn whoever is eating about the first bite.

title: Mushroom Swiss Burger
description: Buttery sauteed mushrooms and nutty Swiss over a seared patty.
steps: Melt 2 tbsp butter over medium-high and add the mushrooms in a single layer. Leave them alone 4 minutes so they brown instead of steaming.
Stir, add the garlic and a pinch of salt, cook 3 more minutes, then set aside.
Form and season 4 dimpled patties. Cook in the same pan 3 minutes per side.
Top each with Swiss, pile on the mushrooms, cover the pan and cook 1 minute to melt.
Toast the buns in the remaining butter and spread with mayo.
Assemble and serve hot.

title: Turkey Burgers
description: Leaner burgers kept moist with grated onion and a little mayo in the mix.
steps: Squeeze the grated onion in a paper towel to remove excess water, then mix it with the turkey, mayo, Worcestershire, garlic powder, salt and pepper. Mix just until combined.
Form 4 patties and chill them 10 minutes if you have time - turkey is soft and holds its shape better cold.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium. Cook 5-6 minutes per side until the centers reach 165F.
Add provolone in the last minute and cover to melt.
Toast the buns, then build with lettuce and tomato.

title: Black Bean Burgers
description: A vegetarian patty from two pantry cans that actually holds together and tastes smoky.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) black beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Spread the drained beans on a sheet pan and bake at 325F for 15 minutes to dry them out. This single step is what keeps the patties from turning to mush.
Mash about three quarters of the beans with a fork, leaving the rest whole for texture.
Mix in the breadcrumbs, egg, onion, garlic, cumin, chili powder, salt and pepper. Form 4 firm patties.
Heat the oil over medium and cook 5-6 minutes per side until a crust forms. Do not move them early.
Add the pepper jack in the last minute and cover to melt.
Serve on toasted buns with whatever condiments you like.

title: BBQ Bacon Burger
description: Barbecue sauce, bacon, cheddar and crisp fried onions piled on one patty.
steps: Render the bacon in a cold skillet over medium heat until crisp, then drain, leaving 1 tbsp of fat in the pan.
Form and season 4 dimpled patties.
Cook 3 minutes, flip, brush the cooked side with barbecue sauce, add cheddar and cook 3 minutes more.
Toast the buns in the pan.
Spread more barbecue sauce on the bottom bun, then stack lettuce, patty, bacon and a handful of fried onions.

title: Sloppy Joes
description: Sweet-tangy ground beef simmered in 15 minutes and spooned onto soft buns.
steps: Brown the beef in a large skillet over medium-high, breaking it up, about 6 minutes. Drain off most of the fat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook 5 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the ketchup, brown sugar, mustard, Worcestershire, salt and pepper.
Simmer uncovered 8-10 minutes until thick enough to mound on a spoon.
Taste and adjust - more mustard for tang, more sugar for sweetness. Spoon onto toasted buns.

title: Chili Cheese Dogs
description: Griddled hot dogs under quick beef chili, shredded cheddar and raw onion.
ingredients: 1 yellow onion, half diced half reserved raw
steps: Brown the beef with the diced half of the onion over medium-high, about 7 minutes, breaking the meat up fine. Pour off the fat.
Stir in the chili powder and cumin and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomato sauce, water and salt, then simmer 12-15 minutes until thick and scoopable, not soupy.
Griddle the hot dogs in a dry skillet, turning, until blistered and heated through, 5 minutes.
Warm the buns, add a dog, a line of mustard, a generous spoon of chili, cheddar and raw diced onion.

title: Pigs in a Blanket
description: Cocktail franks rolled in crescent dough - the easiest party food there is.
ingredients: 1 package (8 oz) refrigerated crescent roll dough
steps: Heat the oven to 375F and line a sheet pan with parchment.
Unroll the dough and cut each triangle lengthwise into 3 thin triangles.
Roll a frank up in each triangle starting at the wide end. Place seam-side down on the pan, an inch apart.
Brush with melted butter and scatter the sesame and poppy seeds over the top.
Bake 13-15 minutes until deep golden. Serve warm with mustard and ketchup.

title: Pan-Seared Ribeye
description: Butter-basted ribeye with a hard crust - the steakhouse method in one skillet.
ingredients: 2 ribeye steaks, 1 1/4 inch thick (about 12 oz each)
steps: Salt the steaks on all sides and leave them uncovered on a rack at room temperature for 40 minutes. A dry surface is the difference between a crust and gray meat.
Pat completely dry and add the pepper. Heat the oil in a cast-iron skillet over high until it shimmers and just smokes.
Lay the steaks in away from you and do not touch them for 3 minutes.
Flip, add the butter, garlic and thyme, and tilt the pan to spoon the foaming butter over the steaks for 2-3 minutes.
Pull at 125F internal for medium-rare, 135F for medium. Use a thermometer - thickness varies more than time does.
Rest on a board 8 minutes before slicing against the grain. Spoon the pan butter over the slices.

title: Garlic Butter Sirloin
description: An affordable steak that eats like an expensive one, finished with garlic butter.
ingredients: 2 lb top sirloin steak, 1 inch thick
steps: Mash the softened butter with the garlic and parsley and set it aside.
Pat the steak very dry and season heavily on both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a heavy skillet over high until smoking. Sear 4 minutes without moving.
Flip and sear 3-4 minutes more, to 130F for medium-rare.
Move to a board, put a spoonful of the garlic butter on top and tent loosely with foil for 7 minutes.
Slice thin against the grain and pour the melted butter and juices from the board over the top.

title: Grilled T-Bone Steak
description: Two cuts on one bone, grilled over two heat zones so both finish together.
steps: Salt the steaks and rest them at room temperature 40 minutes, then pat dry, oil lightly and add pepper.
Build a two-zone fire: coals banked on one side, or half the gas burners on high and half off.
Sear over the hot zone 3 minutes per side, positioning the steaks so the smaller tenderloin side points toward the cooler edge - it cooks faster than the strip.
Move to the cool zone, close the lid and cook to 125F at the thickest point, 6-9 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes with a knob of butter on top.
Cut the strip and tenderloin off the bone, slice both, and squeeze the grilled lemon over.

title: Reverse-Sear Filet Mignon
description: Slow oven first, hard sear last - edge-to-edge pink with no gray band.
ingredients: 4 filet mignon steaks, 2 inches thick (6 oz each)
steps: Salt the steaks all over and set them on a rack over a sheet pan. Refrigerate uncovered at least 1 hour, or up to overnight, to dry the surface.
Heat the oven to 250F. Roast the steaks on the rack until a thermometer reads 115F in the center, 35-45 minutes depending on thickness.
Rest 10 minutes while you heat the oil in a heavy skillet over the highest heat your stove makes.
Pat the steaks dry again and sear 60-75 seconds per side, no longer - they are already cooked, you are only building crust.
Add the butter, garlic and rosemary and baste 30 seconds. Pull at 128F.
Rest 5 minutes and serve whole with the pan butter spooned over.

title: Steak au Poivre
description: Peppercorn-crusted steak with a brandy cream pan sauce - the classic steakhouse order.
ingredients: 4 New York strip steaks (8 oz each)
2 tbsp whole black peppercorns, coarsely crushed
steps: Crush the peppercorns under a heavy pan - you want cracked pieces, not powder. Salt the steaks, then press the pepper firmly onto both sides.
Sear in oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high, 4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the butter and shallots and cook 2 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat before adding the brandy - it can flare. Return it to the heat and let it bubble down by half, about 1 minute.
Stir in the cream and Dijon and simmer 3-4 minutes until the sauce coats a spoon. Add any resting juices.
Spoon the sauce over the rested steaks.

title: Flank Steak with Chimichurri
description: Fast-grilling flank steak with a raw herb sauce you stir together in two minutes.
steps: Stir the parsley, garlic, vinegar, olive oil, oregano, pepper flakes and 1/2 tsp salt together. Let the chimichurri sit while you cook - it improves.
Pat the steak dry and season both sides hard with the rest of the salt and the pepper.
Grill or pan-sear over the highest heat, 4-5 minutes per side for medium-rare. Flank is thin and goes from perfect to tough fast.
Rest 10 minutes. Skipping this on flank costs you most of the juice.
Find the direction of the long muscle fibers and slice thinly straight across them at a slight angle.
Spoon the chimichurri over the slices.

title: Salisbury Steak
description: Seasoned beef patties in onion-mushroom gravy, spooned over mashed potatoes.
steps: Mix the beef, breadcrumbs, egg, Worcestershire, onion powder, 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Form 4 oval patties about 3/4 inch thick.
Brown the patties in the butter over medium-high, 3 minutes per side. Move them to a plate - they are not cooked through yet.
Add the onion and mushrooms to the pan and cook 8 minutes until browned and the liquid has gone.
Sprinkle the flour over and stir 1 minute, then whisk in the broth a little at a time so it stays smooth.
Return the patties, lower the heat, cover and simmer 12-15 minutes, turning once, until the gravy thickens and the patties are cooked through.
Season the gravy and serve over mashed potatoes or egg noodles.

title: Chicken Fried Steak
description: Tenderized cube steak in a craggy crust under black pepper cream gravy.
steps: Mix the flour with the salt, 1 tsp pepper, garlic powder and cayenne in one dish. Beat the eggs with the buttermilk in another.
Pat the steaks dry. Dredge in flour, then buttermilk, then flour again, pressing hard so the coating grips. Rest on a rack 10 minutes - this sets the crust.
Heat 1/2 inch of oil to 350F in a heavy skillet. Too cool and it turns greasy, too hot and the crust burns before the meat cooks.
Fry 2 steaks at a time, 3-4 minutes per side, until deep golden. Drain on a rack, not paper towels, so the bottom stays crisp.
Pour off all but 1/4 cup of the oil. Whisk in 1/4 cup of the leftover dredging flour and cook 2 minutes until it smells toasty.
Whisk in the milk slowly and simmer 4-5 minutes to a pourable gravy. Add lots of black pepper and pour over the steaks.

title: Philly Cheesesteak
description: Shaved ribeye, onions and melted provolone packed into a long roll.
steps: Freeze the steak 30-45 minutes until firm, then slice it as thinly as you possibly can. Partial freezing is the only way to get paper-thin slices at home.
Cook the onions and pepper in 1 tbsp oil over medium-high for 8 minutes until soft and browned at the edges. Push them to one side of the pan.
Add the rest of the oil and the beef to the empty side. Cook 2-3 minutes, chopping it up with the edge of your spatula as it browns.
Season, mix the meat and vegetables together, and divide into 4 piles in the pan.
Lay 2 slices of provolone on each pile and let them melt, 1 minute.
Scoop each pile, cheese side up, straight into a roll.

title: Steak and Eggs
description: A high-protein breakfast plate: quick-seared steak with eggs fried in the same pan.
steps: Pat the steaks dry and season both sides well.
Sear in the oil over high heat, 3 minutes per side for medium-rare. Move to plates to rest.
Lower the heat to medium, add the butter and let the foam subside.
Crack in the eggs and fry 2-3 minutes, spooning butter over the whites, until the edges are crisp and the yolks still run.
Slide the eggs onto the steaks, spoon over the pan butter and finish with chives and more black pepper.

title: Slow Cooker Pulled Pork
description: Pork shoulder cooked to shreds all day, then tossed with barbecue sauce.
steps: Mix the brown sugar, paprika, salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder and cayenne. Rub it over every surface of the pork.
Put the pork in the slow cooker fat side up and pour the broth around it, not over it, so the rub stays on.
Cook on low 8-10 hours. It is ready when a fork twists in the meat with no resistance - time matters less than that test.
Move the pork to a board and pour the cooking liquid into a bowl. Let the fat rise and skim it off.
Shred with two forks, discarding large fat pieces. Return the meat to the cooker.
Add the barbecue sauce and 1/2 cup of the skimmed cooking liquid and toss. Pile onto buns with coleslaw.

title: Oven Baby Back Ribs
description: Low-and-slow ribs in foil, finished under the broiler with sticky sauce. No smoker needed.
steps: Heat the oven to 275F. Slide a knife under the thin membrane on the bone side of each rack and pull it off with a paper towel - it never gets tender.
Mix the rub and massage it into both sides of the ribs.
Wrap each rack tightly in foil, set on a sheet pan and bake 2.5 hours until the meat pulls back from the bone ends.
Open the foil carefully - the steam is hot - and pour off the liquid.
Brush the ribs generously with barbecue sauce and broil 4-6 inches from the element for 4-6 minutes, watching constantly, until the sauce bubbles and chars at the edges.
Rest 10 minutes, then cut between the bones.

title: BBQ Chicken Thighs
description: Bone-in thighs grilled skin-down, sauced only at the end so nothing burns.
steps: Pat the thighs very dry and toss with the salt, pepper, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder and cayenne.
Set up a two-zone fire: one side hot, one side with no heat under it.
Start the thighs skin-side down over the cooler zone, lid closed, for 20 minutes. Fat renders out and the skin tightens without flaring.
Flip and cook 5-8 minutes more until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 175F. Dark meat is better at 175F than at 165F.
Brush both sides with barbecue sauce and move over the hot zone for 2-3 minutes per side, just long enough to caramelize. Any earlier and the sugar burns.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.

title: Smoked Beef Brisket
description: The hardest thing in barbecue: 12 hours of fire management for bark and a tender slice.
steps: Trim the fat cap to a quarter inch and remove the hard fat seam between the point and the flat. Smear thinly with mustard so the rub sticks.
Mix the salt, pepper and garlic powder and coat every surface heavily. Rest at room temperature 1 hour.
Bring the smoker to a steady 250F with oak or hickory. Place the brisket fat-side up and close the lid.
Smoke 6-8 hours until the bark is dark and set and the internal temperature reaches about 165F. It will stall there for hours - that is evaporative cooling, not a problem.
Wrap tightly in butcher paper or foil with the broth and continue to 203F internal, 4-6 more hours. Probe for feel: the thermometer should slide in like warm butter.
Rest wrapped in a cooler at least 2 hours - this is as important as the cook. Slice the flat against the grain pencil-thick, then turn 90 degrees to slice the point.

title: BBQ Glazed Meatloaf
description: A moist loaf with a sticky barbecue glaze baked on top.
steps: Heat the oven to 375F. Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes - this is what keeps the loaf from drying out.
Mix in the beef, eggs, onion, garlic, Worcestershire, salt and pepper with your hands until just combined. Overworking it makes the texture rubbery.
Shape into a free-form loaf on a foil-lined sheet pan rather than packing it into a pan - more surface browns that way.
Bake 40 minutes. Stir the barbecue sauce with the brown sugar and brush half over the loaf.
Bake 20 more minutes, brushing on the rest halfway, until the center reads 160F.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing thick.

title: Grilled Corn on the Cob
description: Charred sweet corn with herb butter - five minutes of work.
steps: Heat the grill to medium-high. Mash the butter with the salt, pepper and parsley.
Put the corn directly on the grate with nothing on it. Oil or butter now would just burn.
Grill 10-12 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, until charred in spots on all sides and the kernels are glossy.
Roll each hot ear in the herb butter so it melts into the kernels.
Serve with lime wedges.

title: Baked Beans
description: Canned beans doctored with bacon, molasses and mustard into a proper side.
ingredients: 3 cans (15 oz each) navy beans, drained
steps: Heat the oven to 325F. Cook the bacon in an oven-safe pot over medium until the fat renders, 6 minutes.
Add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in everything else along with 1/2 cup water.
Bake uncovered 50-60 minutes, stirring once, until the sauce is thick and darkened at the edges.
Let it sit 10 minutes before serving - it thickens further as it cools.

title: Creamy Coleslaw
description: Crunchy cabbage slaw in a tangy-sweet dressing. Better after an hour in the fridge.
steps: Toss the shredded cabbage with 1/2 tsp of the salt and leave it in a colander for 15 minutes, then squeeze gently. This keeps the finished slaw from going watery.
Whisk the mayonnaise, vinegar, sugar, Dijon, celery seed, remaining salt and pepper until smooth.
Toss the cabbage and carrots in the dressing until evenly coated.
Chill at least 1 hour. Taste again before serving and add vinegar if it needs sharpening.

title: Classic Potato Salad
description: Creamy mustard-mayo potato salad with celery, onion and hard-boiled egg.
ingredients: 3 lb Yukon gold potatoes, cut in 1-inch chunks
steps: Put the potatoes in cold salted water, bring to a boil and simmer 12-15 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Starting in cold water cooks them evenly.
Boil the eggs in a separate pot 10 minutes, then cool in ice water, peel and chop.
Drain the potatoes and, while they are still hot, toss with the vinegar. Hot potatoes absorb it; cold ones do not.
Let them cool 15 minutes, then fold in the mayonnaise, mustard, celery, onion, pickle, eggs, salt and pepper.
Chill at least 1 hour. Dust with paprika before serving.

title: Baked Mac and Cheese
description: A real cheese sauce baked under a buttered crumb top. No powdered packet.
steps: Heat the oven to 375F. Boil the macaroni 2 minutes short of the package time - it finishes in the oven.
Melt 4 tbsp butter in a large pot, whisk in the flour and cook 2 minutes until it smells nutty but stays pale.
Whisk in the warm milk in a slow stream and simmer 4-5 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon. Add the mustard powder, garlic powder, cayenne, salt and pepper.
Take the pot off the heat before adding the cheese, a handful at a time. Direct heat makes cheese sauce grainy.
Fold in the pasta and pour into a buttered 9x13 dish. Toss the panko with the last of the melted butter and scatter over the top.
Bake 25-30 minutes until bubbling at the edges and golden on top. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

title: Skillet Cornbread
description: Cast-iron cornbread with a crackling crust from preheating the pan.
steps: Put a 10-inch cast-iron skillet in the oven and heat to 425F. A ripping-hot pan is what gives cornbread its crust.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder and salt together.
In another bowl whisk the buttermilk, eggs and 3 tbsp of the melted butter.
Pour the wet into the dry and stir just until combined - lumps are fine, overmixing makes it tough.
Take the hot skillet out, swirl in the remaining butter, then pour in the batter. It should sizzle.
Bake 22-25 minutes until the top is golden and a toothpick comes out clean. Serve from the pan.

title: Buffalo Wings
description: Baking powder is the trick: oven wings that crisp like fried, tossed in hot butter sauce.
ingredients: 3 lb chicken wings, split at the joint
steps: Heat the oven to 250F. Pat the wings bone dry and toss with the baking powder, salt, pepper and garlic powder. Use baking powder, not baking soda.
Arrange on a rack set in a sheet pan and bake on a low shelf 30 minutes to render the fat.
Raise the heat to 425F, move the pan to a high shelf and bake 20-25 minutes more until blistered and deep golden.
Whisk the hot sauce, melted butter and vinegar together in a large bowl.
Add the hot wings and toss immediately - they absorb the sauce best straight out of the oven.
Serve with blue cheese dressing and celery.

title: Beer Can Chicken
description: A whole chicken roasted upright over an open can so the skin crisps all the way around.
steps: Set up a grill for indirect medium heat, about 350F, with no burner directly under where the bird will sit.
Pat the chicken completely dry, rub with oil, then coat inside and out with the mixed salt and spices.
Open the beer, pour out or drink a third, and set the can on a stable tray. Lower the chicken over it so it stands upright with the legs forward.
Set it on the cool zone, close the lid and cook 70-85 minutes without opening it more than you must.
It is done when the thickest part of the thigh reads 175F and the breast 160F.
Lift carefully - the can is full of scalding liquid - rest 10 minutes, then carve.

title: Buttermilk Pancakes
description: Tall, tender pancakes from one bowl. Lumps in the batter are a feature.
ingredients: 4 tbsp butter, melted, plus more for the pan
steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl beat the buttermilk, eggs and melted butter.
Pour the wet into the dry and fold about 10 strokes. Stop while it is still lumpy - overmixing is the only way to ruin these.
Let the batter sit 5 minutes while the pan heats over medium-low. Patience here gives you height.
Butter the pan and ladle in 1/3 cup portions. Cook until bubbles break on the surface and the edges look dry, 2-3 minutes, then flip and cook 1-2 minutes more.
Serve in stacks with butter and warm maple syrup.

title: Belgian Waffles
description: Crisp outside, custardy inside, from whipped egg whites folded in at the end.
steps: Heat the waffle iron. Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt together.
Whisk the milk, egg yolks, melted butter and vanilla, then stir into the dry ingredients until just smooth.
Beat the egg whites in a clean bowl until they hold soft peaks - this is what makes the inside light.
Fold the whites into the batter in two additions with a spatula, stopping while a few streaks remain.
Cook about 3/4 cup of batter per waffle until the iron stops steaming and the waffle is deep golden, 4-5 minutes.
Keep finished waffles on a rack in a 200F oven rather than stacked, so they stay crisp. Serve with syrup.

title: French Toast
description: Thick bread soaked in vanilla custard and griddled in butter.
ingredients: 8 thick slices day-old brioche or Texas toast
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and salt in a wide dish until completely blended with no streaks of white.
Soak each slice 20 seconds per side. Stale, thick bread takes the custard without falling apart; fresh sandwich bread turns to mush.
Melt 1 tbsp butter in a skillet over medium. Cook 2 slices at a time, 3 minutes per side, until deep golden and no longer wet in the middle.
Wipe the pan and add fresh butter between batches so the milk solids do not burn.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve with warm maple syrup.

title: Biscuits and Sausage Gravy
description: Peppery sausage cream gravy over split buttermilk biscuits.
ingredients: 1/4 cup all-purpose flour, for the gravy
steps: Heat the oven to 450F. Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt, then cut in the cold butter with your fingers until you have pea-sized pieces. Visible butter is what makes biscuits flaky.
Stir in the buttermilk until a shaggy dough forms. Pat it out, fold it over on itself three times, then cut rounds and bake 12-14 minutes until risen and golden.
Meanwhile brown the sausage in a skillet over medium-high, breaking it into crumbles, 7 minutes. Leave all the fat in the pan.
Sprinkle the flour over the sausage and stir 2 minutes until no dry flour remains.
Pour in the milk gradually, scraping the pan, and simmer 5-8 minutes until it thickens to a gravy. It will thicken more off the heat.
Season heavily with black pepper and salt, then ladle over split biscuits.

title: Crispy Hash Browns
description: A golden potato cake - the whole secret is squeezing the water out.
ingredients: 2 lb russet potatoes, peeled and grated
steps: Put the grated potato in a clean kitchen towel and wring it out hard over the sink. Do it twice. The amount of water that comes out is the difference between crisp and soggy.
Toss the dried shreds with the salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Heat the butter and oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium until the butter stops foaming.
Add the potatoes and press into an even layer with a spatula. Cook 7-8 minutes without touching them.
Loosen the edges, slide the cake onto a plate, invert it back into the pan and cook 6-7 minutes on the second side.
Slide onto a rack for a minute so the bottom stays crisp, then cut in wedges.

title: Corned Beef Hash
description: Crisped potatoes and corned beef with eggs cooked right in the pan.
steps: Parboil the diced potatoes in salted water 5 minutes, then drain well and let them steam dry.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add the potatoes in one layer and leave them 5 minutes to brown before stirring.
Add the onion and pepper and cook 5 minutes, then the corned beef, salt, pepper and paprika.
Press everything flat and let it sit 4-5 minutes to build a crust on the bottom, then fold it over once.
Make 4 wells with the back of a spoon, crack in the eggs, cover and cook 4 minutes for runny yolks.
Scatter parsley over and serve from the pan.

title: Cheese Omelette
description: Three eggs, low heat, soft curds and a cheese center. Five minutes.
steps: Beat the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper for a full 30 seconds until completely uniform in color.
Melt the butter in an 8-inch nonstick pan over medium-low. It should foam, not brown.
Pour in the eggs and let them set 20 seconds, then stir slowly with a spatula, pushing the set curds in from the edges.
When the eggs are mostly set but still glossy on top, stop stirring and smooth the surface.
Scatter the cheese over one half and cook 30 seconds more.
Fold the empty half over and slide onto a plate. Top with chives. A proper omelette is pale yellow, not brown.

title: Eggs Benedict
description: Poached eggs and Canadian bacon on muffins under blender hollandaise.
steps: Make the hollandaise first, since it waits better than eggs do. Blend the yolks, lemon juice, salt and cayenne 20 seconds.
With the blender running, pour the hot melted butter in a very thin stream. Going slowly is the whole technique - rushing breaks the sauce. Keep it somewhere warm, not hot.
Bring a wide pan of water to a bare simmer and add the vinegar. Toast the muffins and warm the Canadian bacon in a dry skillet.
Crack each egg into a fine strainer first and let the loose white drain away. This is why restaurant poached eggs look neat.
Slip the eggs into the water and poach 3 minutes for a runny yolk. Lift out with a slotted spoon onto a towel.
Stack muffin, bacon, egg, then a generous spoonful of hollandaise. Finish with chives and cayenne.

title: Egg and Cheese Breakfast Sandwich
description: Folded egg, sausage and melted American cheese on a toasted muffin.
steps: Cook the sausage patties in a skillet over medium 3 minutes per side until browned through. Toast the muffins.
Wipe the pan, lower the heat and melt the butter.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper, pour into the pan and let them set 1 minute.
Fold the egg in from all four sides to make two squares roughly the size of the muffins, then flip and cook 30 seconds.
Lay cheese on the hot egg to melt, then build: muffin, sausage, egg and cheese, muffin.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
description: Buttermilk-brined chicken in a shatteringly crisp seasoned crust.
ingredients: 1 tbsp kosher salt, for the brine
steps: Whisk the buttermilk, hot sauce and kosher salt and submerge the chicken. Refrigerate at least 3 hours, ideally overnight.
Mix the flour with the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper and cayenne. Add 3 tbsp of the brine to the flour and rub it in - those shaggy bits become the crunchiest crust.
Lift each piece from the brine, let it drip briefly, then press firmly into the flour. Rest on a rack 15 minutes so the coating hydrates and grips.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 325F in a heavy pot. Use a thermometer - this is the step people get wrong.
Fry in batches of 3-4, never crowding, 12-16 minutes, turning once. Adjust the burner to hold 300-325F. Breasts finish at 160F, thighs and drums at 175F.
Drain on a rack and salt immediately. Let the oil recover to 325F between batches.

title: Crispy Chicken Tenders
description: Panko-crusted tenders baked hot instead of fried, with honey mustard.
steps: Heat the oven to 425F with a rack set in a sheet pan. Toss the panko with the oil in a bowl until evenly moistened - dry panko bakes pale, oiled panko browns like fried.
Season the chicken, then set up three dishes: flour, beaten egg, oiled panko.
Coat each tender in flour, then egg, then press into the panko.
Arrange on the rack with space between them and bake 18-20 minutes until deep golden and 165F inside.
Stir the honey, Dijon and mayo together for dipping.

title: Chicken and Waffles
description: Fried chicken on a waffle with hot honey - the sweet-savory brunch plate.
steps: Soak the chicken in the buttermilk and hot sauce at least 1 hour.
Warm the honey with the red pepper flakes in a small pan for 2 minutes, then take it off the heat to steep.
Mix the flour, paprika, salt, pepper and cayenne. Dredge each piece straight from the buttermilk, pressing hard.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 340F and fry in batches 6-8 minutes until deep golden and 175F inside. Drain on a rack and salt right away.
Cook the waffles while the chicken drains so both are hot at once.
Set chicken on each waffle, add a pat of butter and pour the hot honey over.

title: Club Sandwich
description: Triple-decker turkey, bacon, lettuce and tomato, cut into quarters.
steps: Cook the bacon until crisp and drain. Toast all 6 slices of bread.
Spread mayonnaise on one side of 2 slices, both sides of 2 slices, and one side of the last 2.
Build each sandwich: bottom slice, lettuce, turkey, tomato, salt and pepper, then a middle slice mayo-side up, then bacon, more lettuce and the top slice.
Press down gently and spear each quarter with a toothpick before cutting, or the whole thing slides apart.
Cut diagonally into 4 triangles.

title: BLT
description: Three ingredients done right: crisp bacon, ripe tomato, cold lettuce, good mayo.
steps: Lay the bacon in a cold skillet and cook over medium, turning once, until evenly crisp - about 10 minutes. Starting cold renders the fat before the meat burns.
Toast the bread while the bacon drains on paper towels.
Salt the tomato slices and let them sit a minute. Seasoning the tomato, not just the sandwich, is what makes a BLT taste like more than bread.
Spread mayonnaise on all four slices of toast, right to the edges.
Stack lettuce, tomato, pepper and 4 slices of bacon per sandwich, then cut in half and eat immediately.

title: Grilled Cheese
description: Mayo on the outside, two cheeses inside, low and slow for even browning.
steps: Spread a thin layer of mayonnaise on the outside face of each slice. It browns more evenly than butter and will not burn.
Divide both cheeses between two sandwiches. Shredded cheese melts far faster than sliced.
Set the sandwiches mayo-side down in a cold nonstick pan, then turn the heat to medium-low.
Cook 4-5 minutes until deep golden, pressing gently with a spatula.
Flip, add the butter to the pan beside the sandwich, and cook 4 more minutes until the cheese is fully molten.
Rest 1 minute before cutting so the cheese does not run out.

title: Tuna Melt
description: Tuna salad and cheddar griddled on buttered bread until the cheese runs.
ingredients: 2 cans (5 oz each) tuna in water, drained well
steps: Press the tuna in a strainer to get the water out, then flake it with a fork.
Mix with the mayonnaise, celery, onion, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Butter the outsides of the bread. Build each sandwich with cheese, tuna salad, then cheese again - cheese on both sides glues it together.
Griddle over medium-low 4 minutes per side, pressing lightly, until golden and fully melted.
Cut in half and serve hot.

title: Reuben Sandwich
description: Corned beef, sauerkraut, Swiss and Russian dressing griddled on rye.
ingredients: 1 cup sauerkraut, drained and squeezed dry
steps: Stir the mayonnaise, ketchup and relish together for the Russian dressing.
Squeeze the sauerkraut hard in a towel. Wet kraut makes a soggy Reuben.
Warm the corned beef briefly in a dry skillet so it is not cold in the middle.
Butter the outsides of the bread. Layer: Swiss, corned beef, sauerkraut, dressing, Swiss.
Griddle over medium-low 4-5 minutes per side, pressing with a spatula, until the bread is dark gold and the cheese has melted into the meat.

title: French Dip
description: Thin roast beef on a crusty roll with a bowl of hot au jus for dunking.
steps: Cook the onion in the butter over medium 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the broth, Worcestershire and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes to concentrate.
Dip the sliced beef in the hot jus for 20 seconds, just to warm it through - do not let it cook or it toughens.
Pile the beef into the rolls, top with provolone and broil 2 minutes until bubbling.
Strain the jus into small bowls and serve alongside for dipping.

title: Classic Pot Roast
description: Chuck roast braised with carrots and potatoes until it falls apart.
steps: Heat the oven to 325F. Pat the roast dry and season all over.
Sear it in the oil in a Dutch oven over high heat, 4 minutes per side, until deeply browned. This browning is where most of the flavor comes from, so do not rush it.
Move the meat out and cook the onions 5 minutes. Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir 2 minutes until the paste darkens.
Pour in the wine and scrape the bottom clean, then add the broth, bay leaves and thyme.
Return the roast, cover and braise 2.5 hours. Add the carrots and potatoes and cook 1 hour more, until a fork twists easily in the meat.
Rest 15 minutes, then pull the beef into chunks and serve in the braising liquid.

title: Beef Stew
description: Flour-dredged beef browned hard, then simmered low with root vegetables.
ingredients: 3 lb beef chuck, cut in 1 1/2-inch cubes
steps: Pat the beef dry and toss with the flour, salt and pepper.
Brown the cubes in the oil in batches over medium-high, 3 minutes per side. Crowding the pot steams the meat instead of browning it, so work in batches even though it takes longer.
Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the same pot 6 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Return the beef, add the broth, bay leaves and thyme, and bring to a bare simmer. Cover and cook 1.5 hours at the lowest bubble.
Add the potatoes and cook 30-40 minutes more until the beef shreds under a fork.
Stir in the peas, cook 5 minutes, fish out the bay leaves and season to taste.

title: Chicken Pot Pie
description: Creamy chicken and vegetables under a flaky store-bought crust.
steps: Heat the oven to 400F and line a 9-inch pie dish with one crust.
Melt the butter and cook the onion, carrots and celery 7 minutes until softened.
Add the chicken and cook 5 minutes, then sprinkle over the flour and stir 2 minutes.

Pour in the broth and milk slowly, stirring, and simmer 5 minutes until thick. Add the peas, salt, pepper and thyme. Let the filling cool 10 minutes - hot filling melts the top crust before it can puff.
Fill the pie, lay the second crust over, crimp the edges and cut 4 steam vents. Brush with the beaten egg.
Bake 35-40 minutes until the crust is deep golden. Rest 15 minutes before cutting or it will run.

title: Shepherd's Pie
description: Savory ground beef under a browned mashed potato crust.
ingredients: 2 1/2 lb russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water 15 minutes until tender, then drain and let them steam dry for 2 minutes before mashing with 4 tbsp butter and the warm milk. Season well.
Brown the beef over medium-high 8 minutes and drain the fat. Add the onion and carrots and cook 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and flour and cook 2 minutes, then add the broth and Worcestershire and simmer 8 minutes until thick.
Fold in the peas and season. Spread in a 9x13 dish.
Spoon the mash over in dollops and spread gently to the edges to seal, then rough up the surface with a fork - the ridges are what brown.
Dot with the remaining butter, scatter the cheddar over and bake at 400F for 25-30 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges.

title: Beef Chili
description: Thick beef and bean chili that gets better the longer it simmers.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) kidney beans, drained
steps: Brown the beef in a large pot over medium-high 8 minutes, breaking it up. Drain most of the fat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook 6 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the chili powder, cumin, oregano and cayenne and stir 1 full minute in the hot fat. Blooming the spices this way tastes completely different from dumping them into liquid.
Add the tomatoes, beans, broth, salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer.
Cook uncovered at a low bubble 60 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick enough that a spoon leaves a trail.
Taste and adjust. Serve with cheddar and sour cream.

title: New England Clam Chowder
description: Thick cream chowder with bacon, potatoes and canned clams.
ingredients: 3 cans (6.5 oz each) chopped clams, juice reserved
2 cups clam juice or chicken broth
steps: Render the bacon in a pot over medium until crisp. Lift out the pieces, leaving the fat behind.
Cook the onion and celery in the fat 6 minutes, then stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes.
Whisk in the reserved clam juice and the extra juice or broth gradually so no lumps form. Add the potatoes and thyme.
Simmer 15-18 minutes until the potatoes are tender. Mash a few against the side of the pot to thicken the chowder naturally.
Lower the heat, stir in the cream and the clams and heat through for 3-4 minutes only. Boiling after the clams go in turns them rubbery.
Season, then serve topped with the bacon and parsley.

title: Creamy Tomato Soup
description: Canned tomatoes, butter and cream blended smooth in 30 minutes.
ingredients: 2 cans (28 oz each) whole peeled tomatoes
steps: Melt the butter and cook the onion over medium 8 minutes until soft and sweet, not browned.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the tomatoes with their juice, crushing them with your spoon.
Add the broth, sugar, salt and pepper and simmer 20 minutes uncovered. The sugar is there to offset the acidity of canned tomatoes, not to sweeten the soup.
Blend until completely smooth, either with an immersion blender or in batches. Fill a countertop blender only halfway with hot liquid and vent the lid.
Return to low heat, stir in the cream and basil, and warm through without boiling.
Taste for salt and serve with grilled cheese.

title: Chicken Noodle Soup
description: Rotisserie chicken shortcut soup with egg noodles, ready in half an hour.
steps: Melt the butter and cook the onion, carrots and celery over medium 8 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the broth, thyme and bay leaves. Bring to a boil.
Add the noodles and cook according to the package, usually 7-8 minutes.
Stir in the chicken and heat through 3 minutes. Adding it at the end keeps it from going stringy.
Take out the bay leaves, then add the salt, pepper and lemon juice. The lemon is what makes the broth taste bright instead of flat.
Finish with parsley. If making ahead, cook the noodles separately so they do not swell in the broth.

title: Creamy Mashed Potatoes
description: Fluffy mash with warm cream and a lot of butter. The classic side.
ingredients: 3 lb Yukon gold potatoes, peeled and quartered
steps: Start the potatoes in cold, well-salted water and bring to a boil. Cooking them from cold means the outsides do not turn to mush before the centers are done.
Simmer 18-20 minutes until a knife meets no resistance, then drain and return them to the dry pot over low heat for 1 minute to drive off moisture.
Mash or rice them while hot. Never use a blender or food processor - it makes potato glue.
Fold in the butter a few cubes at a time, then the warm cream. Cold cream makes gluey, cool mash.
Season with the salt and white pepper and top with chives.

title: Oven French Fries
description: Soaked, parboiled and roasted hot for a crisp shell and fluffy middle.
ingredients: 2 1/2 lb russet potatoes, cut in 1/2-inch batons
steps: Soak the cut potatoes in cold water 15 minutes and rinse until the water runs clear. Rinsing off surface starch is what lets them crisp.
Boil them in salted water with the vinegar for 6 minutes. The vinegar keeps the edges intact while the insides soften.
Drain gently and let them air-dry on a towel 5 minutes. Meanwhile heat the oven to 450F with a sheet pan inside.
Toss the dry potatoes with the oil and seasonings, then spread them on the hot pan in a single layer with space between.
Roast 20 minutes, flip, then 15-20 minutes more until deep golden and crisp.
Salt again immediately out of the oven.

title: Beer-Battered Onion Rings
description: Thick sweet onion rings in a light, crackling beer batter.
ingredients: 2 large sweet onions, cut in 1/2-inch rings
steps: Separate the onion rings and toss them with 1/4 cup of the flour. A dry floured surface gives the wet batter something to cling to.
Whisk the rest of the flour with the baking powder, salt, paprika and cayenne, then stir in the cold beer until just combined. Lumps are fine, and cold batter fries crisper.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 360F in a heavy pot.
Dip each ring in the batter, let the excess run off, and lower it into the oil. Fry 4-5 at a time for 2-3 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Drain on a rack and salt immediately. Let the oil come back to 360F between batches or the next round comes out greasy.

title: Loaded Potato Skins
description: Crisp potato shells filled with cheddar, bacon and scallions.
steps: Heat the oven to 400F. Rub the potatoes with oil and salt and bake directly on the rack 60 minutes until the skins are crisp and a knife slides in easily.
Cool 10 minutes, halve lengthwise, and scoop out the flesh leaving a 1/4-inch shell. Save the flesh for mashed potatoes.
Brush the shells inside and out with more oil and season. Bake 10 minutes face-down, then 5 minutes face-up - this double bake is what makes them crisp rather than leathery.
Fill with cheddar and bacon and bake 5 minutes more until melted.
Top with sour cream, scallions and black pepper.

title: Deviled Eggs
description: Creamy mustard-paprika filling piped back into halved eggs.
steps: Lower the eggs into already-boiling water and cook 11 minutes. Starting in hot water makes them far easier to peel than starting cold.
Move them straight to ice water for 5 minutes, then peel under running water.
Halve lengthwise and pop the yolks into a bowl.
Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, salt and pepper until completely smooth - any lumps will clog a piping bag.
Pipe or spoon the filling back into the whites.
Dust with paprika and chives. Best within a few hours.

title: Cobb Salad
description: Rows of chicken, bacon, egg, avocado and blue cheese over romaine.
steps: Shake or whisk the vinegar, olive oil, Dijon, salt and pepper into a dressing.
Spread the chopped romaine over a wide platter rather than a bowl - a Cobb is about the stripes.
Lay the chicken, bacon, eggs, avocado, tomatoes and blue cheese in neat parallel rows over the lettuce.
Bring it to the table whole, then pour over the dressing and toss in front of everyone.
Season again after tossing.

title: Caesar Salad
description: Crisp romaine, garlicky anchovy dressing, Parmesan and homemade croutons.
ingredients: 1/4 cup olive oil, for the croutons
steps: Toss the bread cubes with 1/4 cup olive oil and salt and bake at 400F for 10-12 minutes, shaking once, until golden and dry through.
Mash the anchovies and garlic to a paste with the side of your knife. This is what gives the dressing its savory backbone, and it will not taste fishy.
Whisk in the egg yolks, lemon juice, Dijon and Worcestershire.
Add the 1/2 cup olive oil in a very thin stream while whisking constantly, so the dressing emulsifies and thickens. Pouring too fast breaks it.
Stir in half the Parmesan, the salt and plenty of pepper.
Toss the dry romaine with the dressing, then add the croutons and the rest of the Parmesan. Serve right away.

title: Green Bean Casserole
description: The Thanksgiving standard, built on a real mushroom cream sauce.
steps: Boil the green beans in salted water 5 minutes, then shock them in ice water and drain. They finish cooking in the oven and stay green this way.
Cook the mushrooms in the butter over medium-high 7 minutes until browned and dry, then add the onion for 4 minutes and the garlic for 1.
Stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then whisk in the broth and cream and simmer 5 minutes until thick.
Season, fold in the beans, and spread in a 9x13 dish.
Bake at 375F for 20 minutes, scatter the fried onions over the top, and bake 8-10 minutes more until crisp and bubbling.

title: Roast Turkey
description: Dry-brined turkey with butter under the skin - the Thanksgiving centerpiece.
steps: One to three days ahead, pat the turkey dry and rub the salt, pepper and baking powder over the skin and inside the cavity. Refrigerate uncovered on a rack. This dry brine seasons the meat and dries the skin - it matters more than anything you do on the day.
Take the turkey out 1 hour before roasting. Heat the oven to 425F. Mash the butter with the sage and thyme.
Loosen the breast skin with your fingers and push two thirds of the herb butter underneath, directly onto the meat. Rub the rest over the outside.
Scatter the onions, carrots and celery in a roasting pan, set the turkey on top, and add the broth to the pan.
Roast 30 minutes at 425F, then lower to 325F and roast about 2.5 hours more, until the thickest part of the thigh reads 170F and the breast 157F. Tent the breast with foil if it browns too early.
Rest at least 30 minutes before carving. The breast will coast up to a safe 165F while it rests, and the juices redistribute.

title: Honey Glazed Ham
description: Spiral ham lacquered with honey, brown sugar and mustard.
ingredients: 1 spiral-cut bone-in ham (8 lb), fully cooked
steps: Heat the oven to 325F. Set the ham cut-side down in a roasting pan and pour the pineapple juice around it.
Cover tightly with foil and heat 1 hour. The ham is already cooked - you are only warming it, so covered heat keeps it from drying out.
Simmer the honey, brown sugar, Dijon, butter, cloves and cinnamon in a small pan 5 minutes until syrupy.
Uncover the ham, brush on a third of the glaze and raise the oven to 400F.
Bake 30-40 minutes more, glazing twice, until the surface is lacquered and darkened at the edges and the center reads 140F.
Rest 15 minutes, then slice along the spiral and spoon the pan juices over.

title: Corn Dogs
description: Hot dogs in sweet cornmeal batter, fried on a stick.
steps: Push a skewer most of the way up each hot dog and dry them thoroughly with paper towels. Any moisture makes the batter slide off.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder and salt, then stir in the milk and egg to a thick batter. Pour it into a tall glass - dipping is much easier than rolling.
Heat 3 inches of oil to 360F in a deep pot.
Dip each dog into the batter, turning to coat, lift out and let the excess drip for a second.
Lower into the oil holding the stick, and let it set for 10 seconds before releasing. Fry 3-4 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on a rack and serve with mustard.

title: Lobster Roll
description: Cold lobster salad in a buttered, griddled split-top bun.
steps: Fold the lobster with the mayonnaise, celery, lemon juice, chives, salt and pepper. Keep the pieces large - this should look like lobster, not tuna salad. Chill while you toast.
Butter both flat outer sides of each split-top bun generously.
Griddle the buns over medium 2 minutes per side until crisp and golden. Split-top buns exist for exactly this and are worth seeking out.
Line each bun with lettuce and mound the lobster salad in.
Finish with more chives and a squeeze of lemon. Serve cold filling in a warm bun.

title: Maryland Crab Cakes
description: Almost all crab, barely held together, seared in butter.
ingredients: 1 lb lump crab meat, picked over
steps: Whisk the egg, mayonnaise, Dijon, Worcestershire, Old Bay, lemon juice and parsley together first, then fold in the panko.
Add the crab and fold with a rubber spatula no more than a few times. Every extra stir breaks up the lumps you are paying for.
Form 8 loose cakes and refrigerate 30 minutes. Chilling is the only thing keeping them together in the pan.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the cakes 4-5 minutes per side until deep golden.
Flip only once, with a thin spatula, and do not press down.
Serve with lemon wedges.

title: Shrimp and Grits
description: Cheesy grits under garlicky shrimp in a bacon pan sauce.
steps: Bring the water and salt to a boil, whisk in the grits and lower the heat right away. Cook 20-25 minutes, stirring often, until creamy. Stone-ground grits take time and cannot be rushed.
Beat in the cheddar and butter off the heat, then cover and keep warm.
Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp and set it aside, leaving the fat.
Pat the shrimp dry, season with the paprika and cayenne, and cook in the bacon fat over high heat 90 seconds per side until just pink. Pull them out - they will finish in the sauce.
Add the garlic to the pan for 30 seconds, then the broth and lemon juice, scraping up the browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes.
Return the shrimp and bacon to the sauce for 30 seconds, then spoon over bowls of grits with scallions.

title: Apple Pie
description: Spiced apples in a double crust - the hardest and most rewarding American bake.
ingredients: 3 lb baking apples, peeled and sliced
steps: Pulse or cut the cold butter into the flour, sugar and salt until the largest pieces are the size of peas. Add the ice water a tablespoon at a time until the dough just holds together when squeezed. Visible butter streaks are what make the crust flaky.
Divide in two, flatten into disks, wrap and refrigerate at least 1 hour. Warm dough is unworkable dough.
Toss the apples with the sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, cinnamon and nutmeg and let them sit 30 minutes, then drain off half the liquid that collects. This is the step that prevents a soupy pie.
Roll one disk and line a 9-inch pie plate. Fill with the apples, mounding them high since they shrink.
Roll the second disk over the top, trim, crimp the edges firmly and cut several steam vents. Brush with egg and scatter the coarse sugar.
Bake at 425F for 20 minutes, then 375F for 45-55 minutes until the juices bubble thickly through the vents. Cool at least 3 hours - cutting it warm means it runs.

title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Chewy centers, crisp edges, pools of melted chocolate.
steps: Beat the softened butter with both sugars for a full 3 minutes until pale and fluffy. This aerates the dough and is the difference between flat and thick cookies.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Stir in the flour, baking soda and salt just until the flour disappears, then fold in the chips.
Chill the dough 30 minutes. Cold dough spreads less and tastes deeper.
Scoop golf-ball portions onto lined sheets, well apart, and bake at 375F for 10-12 minutes. Pull them when the edges are set but the centers still look underdone.
Sprinkle with flaky salt and cool on the pan 5 minutes before moving - they finish baking on the hot sheet.

title: Fudgy Brownies
description: One bowl, melted chocolate, a shiny crackled top and a dense center.
steps: Heat the oven to 350F and line an 8x8 pan with parchment, leaving an overhang to lift the brownies out.
Melt the butter and chocolate together over low heat or in short microwave bursts, then let it cool for 5 minutes so it does not scramble the eggs.
Whisk in the sugar hard for 1 minute, then the eggs one at a time and the vanilla. Whisking the eggs in vigorously is what creates the shiny crackly top.
Fold in the flour, cocoa and salt with a spatula, stopping the moment it is combined.
Bake 28-32 minutes. A toothpick should come out with moist crumbs, not clean - clean means overbaked.
Cool completely in the pan before lifting out and cutting with a hot, dry knife.

title: Pecan Pie
description: A dark, sticky corn syrup custard under a layer of toasted pecans.
steps: Heat the oven to 350F. Fit the crust into a 9-inch pie plate and crimp the edge.
Toast the pecans on a dry sheet pan 6 minutes until fragrant. Raw pecans taste flat by comparison.
Whisk the eggs, corn syrup, brown sugar, melted butter, vanilla and salt until completely smooth, but stop as soon as it is - whisking in air causes the filling to crack.
Scatter the pecans in the shell and pour the filling over. They will float into an even layer on their own.
Bake 50-60 minutes until the edges are set and the center jiggles like gelatin rather than liquid.
Cool at least 4 hours. The filling sets as it cools, and a warm pecan pie is a puddle.

title: Pumpkin Pie
description: Spiced pumpkin custard in a crust, from one can and five minutes of whisking.
steps: Heat the oven to 425F and line a 9-inch pie plate with the crust.
Whisk the pumpkin, brown sugar, eggs, evaporated milk, spices and salt until uniform.
Pour into the shell and bake 15 minutes at 425F, then lower to 350F and bake 35-40 minutes more.
It is done when the outer two inches are set and the center two inches still wobble. Baking until the middle is firm gives you a cracked, grainy pie.
Cool completely at room temperature, then chill 2 hours before serving with whipped cream.

title: New York Cheesecake
description: Dense, tall and creamy, baked in a water bath to keep it crack-free.
ingredients: 32 oz cream cheese, at room temperature
steps: Mix the graham crumbs, melted butter and 1/4 cup sugar, press firmly into a 9-inch springform pan and bake at 325F for 10 minutes. Wrap the outside of the pan in heavy foil.
Beat the room-temperature cream cheese alone for 3 minutes until perfectly smooth. Cold cream cheese leaves lumps that never disappear.
Add the sugar and beat 2 minutes, then the eggs one at a time on low speed. Beating air in now causes cracks later.
Mix in the sour cream, vanilla, lemon juice and salt until just combined.
Pour into the crust, set the pan inside a roasting pan and pour boiling water halfway up the sides. The water bath is what keeps the texture silky.
Bake 75-85 minutes until the outside is set and the center 3 inches still wobble. Turn the oven off and leave the door ajar for 1 hour, then chill at least 6 hours before unmolding.

title: Carrot Cake
description: Spiced oil-based layers with tangy cream cheese frosting.
steps: Heat the oven to 350F and line two 9-inch round pans. Whisk the flour, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt.
Whisk the oil, both sugars, eggs and vanilla until smooth, then stir in the dry ingredients just until combined. Oil rather than butter is why carrot cake stays moist for days.
Fold in the carrots and walnuts and divide between the pans.
Bake 32-38 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pans 10 minutes, then turn out onto racks and cool completely - frosting a warm cake melts it off.
Beat the cream cheese and butter until smooth, then add the powdered sugar a cup at a time until fluffy.
Stack the layers with frosting between and over the top, then chill 30 minutes before slicing.

title: Banana Bread
description: One bowl, overripe bananas, no mixer needed.
steps: Heat the oven to 350F and grease a 9x5 loaf pan. Use the blackest bananas you have - firm yellow ones have neither the sweetness nor the flavor.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl, then stir in the melted butter, brown sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Add the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt and fold with a spatula until the flour just disappears. Overmixing makes it tough and tunneled.
Pour into the pan and bake 55-65 minutes until a skewer in the center comes out clean. Tent with foil if the top darkens early.
Cool in the pan 15 minutes, then turn out onto a rack. It slices much more cleanly once fully cool.

title: Vanilla Milkshake
description: Thick diner-style shake from three ingredients in a blender.
ingredients: 4 cups vanilla ice cream, slightly softened
steps: Let the ice cream sit out 5 minutes so it blends without needing extra milk.
Put the ice cream, milk and vanilla in the blender, milk first so the blades can catch.
Blend in short pulses, scraping down as needed, until just smooth. Over-blending melts it thin.
Pour into chilled glasses, top with whipped cream and a cherry, and serve with a straw and a spoon.

title: S'mores
description: Toasted marshmallow and chocolate pressed between graham crackers.
ingredients: 2 milk chocolate bars, broken in squares
steps: Set a square of chocolate on half of each graham cracker.
Toast the marshmallows over a fire or under the broiler, turning constantly, until puffed and browned all over. Flames mean char, not toast - keep them just off the flame.
Set a hot marshmallow on the chocolate and cap with the second cracker half.
Press gently and wait 30 seconds so the residual heat melts the chocolate.

title: Banana Split
description: Three scoops over a split banana with three sauces and a cherry.
steps: Chill two long dishes in the freezer for a few minutes while you gather everything - a cold dish buys you several minutes before it all melts.
Lay a split banana along each dish, cut sides facing in.
Set the three scoops in a row between the banana halves.
Spoon chocolate syrup over the vanilla, strawberry sauce over the chocolate and pineapple over the strawberry.
Pipe whipped cream down the length, scatter the peanuts and crown each with a cherry. Serve immediately.

title: Jambalaya
description: One pot of rice, andouille, chicken and shrimp built on the Cajun trinity.
steps: Brown the sausage in the oil in a wide heavy pot, 5 minutes, then the chicken for 5 minutes. Remove both, leaving the fat.
Cook the onion, bell pepper and celery 8 minutes until soft. This trinity is the base of the whole dish.
Add the garlic, Cajun seasoning and thyme for 1 minute, then the tomatoes and cook 3 minutes.
Stir in the rice and toast it 2 minutes, then return the meats and add the broth. Bring to a boil.
Lower to a bare simmer, cover and cook 20 minutes without lifting the lid or stirring. Stirring rice releases starch and turns jambalaya into porridge.
Scatter the shrimp over the top, cover again and cook 5-7 minutes until pink. Rest 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and top with scallions.

title: Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
description: Built on a dark roux stirred patiently for 40 minutes. Nothing shortcuts it.
steps: Make the roux first and give it your full attention. Whisk the oil and flour together in a heavy pot over medium-low and stir constantly for 35-45 minutes until it is the color of milk chocolate. If it smells burnt or shows black flecks, throw it out and start over - burnt roux ruins the whole pot.
Add the onion, pepper and celery straight into the hot roux. It will hiss violently. Cook 8 minutes, then add the garlic.
Whisk in the broth a cup at a time, keeping it smooth, then add the Cajun seasoning, bay leaves and cayenne.
Add the sausage and chicken and simmer uncovered 1 hour, skimming any oil that rises.
Add the okra and cook 30 minutes more, until the gumbo coats a spoon.
Fish out the bay leaves, taste for salt and heat, and serve over rice with scallions.

title: Fried Green Tomatoes
description: Tart unripe tomatoes in a cornmeal crust with buttermilk dipping sauce.
ingredients: 4 large green tomatoes, sliced 1/2 inch thick
steps: Salt the tomato slices and leave them on paper towels 15 minutes, then blot dry. This draws out water that would otherwise steam the crust off.
Set up three dishes: flour, then the buttermilk beaten with the egg, then the cornmeal mixed with the paprika, cayenne and pepper.
Coat each slice flour, buttermilk, cornmeal, pressing the cornmeal on firmly.
Heat 1/2 inch of oil to 350F and fry in batches 2-3 minutes per side until golden. Do not crowd the pan or the temperature drops.
Drain on a rack and salt right away.
Stir the mayonnaise and hot sauce together and serve alongside.

title: Hush Puppies
description: Savory cornmeal fritters fried into crisp golden balls.
steps: Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and cayenne together.
Stir in the buttermilk, egg and grated onion until just combined, then let the batter rest 10 minutes so the cornmeal hydrates.
Heat 3 inches of oil to 365F.
Drop rounded tablespoons of batter into the oil, 5 or 6 at a time. They will sink, then float and turn themselves.
Fry 3-4 minutes until deep golden all over, then drain on a rack and salt immediately.
Check the first one by breaking it open - if the center is raw, lower the heat slightly and fry the rest a minute longer.

title: Southern Collard Greens
description: Greens braised slowly with smoked meat until silky, with pot likker to sop.
ingredients: 3 lb collard greens, stemmed and chopped
steps: Simmer the ham hocks in the broth with the onion and garlic for 45 minutes to build the pot likker.
Wash the collards in several changes of water - they hold a surprising amount of grit - then strip out the thick stems and chop the leaves.
Add the greens to the pot in batches as they wilt down. They will seem like far too much and then collapse to a quarter of the volume.
Add the vinegar, brown sugar, pepper flakes, salt and pepper and simmer uncovered 45-60 minutes until completely tender. Collards need real time; crisp collards are undercooked collards.
Pull the meat off the hocks, chop it and stir it back in.
Taste and add more vinegar for brightness. Serve with the broth and cornbread.

title: Succotash
description: Corn, lima beans and tomato tossed in butter - a 20-minute summer side.
ingredients: 4 cups corn kernels, fresh or frozen
steps: Melt the butter and cook the onion over medium 5 minutes until translucent.
Add the corn and lima beans and cook 6-8 minutes, stirring, until the corn starts to brown in spots.
Add the tomatoes and cook 2 minutes, just until they begin to slump but still hold their shape.
Pour in the cream, season, and simmer 2 minutes until it thickens slightly around the vegetables.
Take off the heat and stir in the basil.

title: Scalloped Potatoes
description: Thin potato slices baked in garlic cream until the top is bronzed.
ingredients: 3 1/2 lb russet potatoes, sliced 1/8 inch thick
steps: Heat the oven to 375F and butter a 9x13 dish. Slice the potatoes on a mandoline or with a steady hand - even thickness is what makes them cook evenly.
Melt the butter, cook the garlic 30 seconds, then add the cream, milk, salt, pepper and nutmeg and bring to a bare simmer.
Add the potato slices to the pot and simmer gently 8 minutes, stirring carefully. Pre-cooking them in the cream releases starch that thickens the sauce, so it never breaks in the oven.
Pour everything into the dish, spreading the slices into an even layer, and press them down under the liquid.
Scatter the Gruyere over and cover with foil. Bake 40 minutes.
Uncover and bake 25-30 minutes more until deep golden and a knife slides through with no resistance. Rest 20 minutes before serving.

title: Pimento Cheese
description: The pate of the South: sharp cheddar, mayo and pimentos, stirred by hand.
steps: Grate the cheddar yourself from a block. Pre-shredded cheese is coated in starch and will make the spread chalky.
Beat the cream cheese and mayonnaise smooth with a fork.
Fold in the cheddar, pimentos, onion powder, garlic powder, cayenne, pepper and hot sauce. Keep it chunky - this is not supposed to be a puree.
Refrigerate at least 1 hour so the flavors come together.
Serve with crackers, celery, or spread thickly on white bread.

title: Egg Salad Sandwich
description: Chopped hard-boiled eggs with mayo, mustard and celery on soft bread.
steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook 11 minutes, then cool in ice water 5 minutes and peel.
Chop them coarsely - leaving some larger pieces of white gives the salad texture instead of paste.
Fold in the mayonnaise, Dijon, celery, chives, salt, pepper and paprika.
Chill 15 minutes if you have time, then pile onto bread with lettuce and cut in half.

title: Chicken Salad Sandwich
description: Shredded chicken with grapes, celery and toasted pecans on croissants.
steps: Shred the chicken by hand into bite-size pieces rather than cubing it - mayonnaise clings to torn edges.
Fold in the mayonnaise, celery, grapes, pecans, lemon juice, dill, salt and pepper.
Taste and adjust: more lemon if it tastes heavy, more salt if it tastes flat.
Chill 15 minutes, then pile into split croissants. Add the pecans at the last moment if making it ahead, so they stay crunchy.

title: Simple Roast Chicken
description: One bird, high heat, crisp skin. The dish every cook should own.
steps: Pat the chicken completely dry, inside and out, and salt it all over. If you have an hour, leave it uncovered in the fridge - dry skin is crisp skin.
Heat the oven to 425F. Rub the butter over the breast and legs and add the pepper.
Put the lemon halves, garlic and thyme in the cavity and tie the legs together with twine if you have it.
Toss the potatoes with the olive oil and salt and scatter them around the bird in a roasting pan or skillet.
Roast 70-80 minutes, basting the potatoes once with the pan fat, until the thigh reads 175F and the juices from it run clear.
Rest 15 minutes before carving. Pour the pan juices over the carved meat and potatoes.

title: Grilled Pork Chops
description: Brined thick-cut chops grilled to 145F and still juicy.
steps: Stir the salt and 1 tbsp brown sugar into the water until dissolved and submerge the chops for 30 minutes. A short brine is what keeps lean pork from drying out.
Take them out, rinse, and pat very dry. Rub with oil, then the remaining brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, pepper and cayenne.
Set up a two-zone fire. Sear the chops over the hot side 2-3 minutes per side for grill marks.
Move them to the cooler side, close the lid, and cook to 145F internal, 8-12 minutes.
Rest 8 minutes. Pork at 145F with a faint blush in the center is correct and safe - cooking to white is what makes it tough.

title: Tater Tot Hotdish
description: Midwestern casserole: seasoned beef and vegetables under a tater tot roof.
ingredients: 2 cans (10.5 oz each) condensed cream of mushroom soup
steps: Heat the oven to 375F. Brown the beef with the onion over medium-high 10 minutes, then add the garlic and drain the fat.
Stir in the soup, milk, frozen vegetables, salt, pepper and onion powder.
Spread in a 9x13 dish and scatter the cheddar over.
Arrange the tater tots in tight rows over the top, right to the edges. A full single layer crisps; piled tots steam.
Bake 40-45 minutes until the tots are golden and the filling bubbles at the corners. Rest 10 minutes.

title: Chicago-Style Hot Dog
description: Dragged through the garden: seven toppings on a poppy seed bun, never ketchup.
steps: Simmer the hot dogs in water at a bare bubble for 5-7 minutes. Chicago dogs are steamed or simmered, never grilled hard.
Steam the buns above the pot for 1 minute until soft and puffy.
Lay a dog in each bun, then build in this order: mustard, relish, onion, tomato wedges, pickle spear, sport peppers.
Finish with a pinch of celery salt over the top. Do not add ketchup.
